mutant.description: The gate's own DENY arm is the standing control, and it is exercised on every leg rather than run once: every allow-assertion is paired with a deny-assertion, and a dedicated leg asserts that the two differ (cottonwood != 49financial). Without that pairing, a gate that returned the full mode list for every input would satisfy every positive leg. Adversarial inputs were chosen to be the ones a sloppy match would admit: 'COTTONWOOD' (case) and 'cottonwood ' (trailing space) are both DENIED, so the match is exact rather than fuzzy. The TAMPER arm is the mutant for the wiring: a hand-edited persisted 'satellites' from a denied firm is refused by the allowed set the hook is given, and a separate leg asserts the hook is given the GATED set -- because passing the declared set there would leave the tamper refusal vacuous while every other leg still passed.
mutant.expected: Denied firms must return exactly ['models','etfs']; a tampered persisted value must not appear in the allowed set; the gate's output for an allowed firm must DIFFER from its output for a denied firm; and TO-4's diff must contain no mode-declaration module.
mutant.observed: FIRED AS EXPECTED, INCLUDING ONE GENUINE REFUSAL. 6 of 6 denied firms returned exactly ['models','etfs'] including the case and whitespace variants; the tamper value was absent from the denied viewer's allowed set; cottonwood ['models','etfs','satellites'] differs from 49financial ['models','etfs']. AC5.declared-set-untouched FAILED on its first run and was CORRECT to -- it named satelliteSet.ts, which carried an unrelated comment edit in the working tree. The commit was split (705bb9df) rather than the assertion loosened, and the leg then passed. A SEPARATE DEFECT WAS CAUGHT BY RE-RUNNING TO-3's EXERCISE AS A REGRESSION CHECK: its pre-change rev defaulted to HEAD, which stopped meaning 'pre-change' the moment TO-3 landed, so the script died at import rather than comparing the new code to itself. declared_exclusions.reason: SAT-c-2 reads 'SERVER-DERIVED OR SERVER-VALIDATED, NEVER CLIENT-ASSERTED'. The gate satisfies this by reading a SERVER-DERIVED firm (claims from GET /auth/me + bearer; the client does not assert its own firm) rather than by adding a server-side mode endpoint. Recorded explicitly because 'server-derived' is satisfied here by the INPUT's provenance, not by moving the decision -- and moving the decision is what would be required if this were ever meant as an authorization boundary, which SAT-c-3 declares it is not.

surprises: OBSERVATION / INERT -- MY OWN TO-3 COMMIT BROKE MY OWN TO-3 EVIDENCE SCRIPT, and nothing would have reported it until someone tried to reproduce the evidence. satellites-mode-axis-exercise.mjs resolved its pre-change modules from `SAT_BEFORE_REV || 'HEAD'`. That was correct exactly while the work was uncommitted and wrong the instant 7ebe38b0 landed, because HEAD then CONTAINS the change and every before/after control would compare the new code to itself. It happened to die at import instead (the pre-change gridConfig imports './satelliteSet', absent from .before/), so it failed loudly -- but that was luck of the import graph, not design: had TO-3 added no new module it would have gone green while measuring nothing. A default that is right only until your own commit lands is a control with an expiry date on it. Fixed at 375bbc9a by resolving the rev from the repository. Found by re-running the older exercise as a regression check while building TO-4.

OBSERVATION / INERT -- comp-transform ternary-audit and comp-blast are NOT USABLE as evidence on this plane, same as recorded for TO-3: ternary-audit reports 'No string-literal union types found' because PositioningMode lives in shared/bookSet.ts, outside its file+types.ts scope, and comp-blast returns NOT-FOUND for these symbols over its 20,779-node graph. Both are reported as measuring nothing rather than quoted as clean.

OBSERVATION / INERT -- the TO-4 gate depends on ProtectedRoute's loading behaviour, which is a property of another component and not of this file. usePersistentToggle does a LAZY INITIAL READ validated against the allowed set, so if this page could mount before auth resolved, `claims` would be null, the allowed set would be the two-pill set, and a legitimate Cottonwood viewer's stored 'satellites' would be REJECTED AND CLEARED on every load. It does not happen because ProtectedRoute.tsx:24 renders a LoadingOverlay while isLoading, so the page does not mount until auth has resolved. Written into the code as a stated dependency rather than left as a property that happens to hold -- a change to ProtectedRoute's loading behaviour would silently start clearing legitimate viewers' remembered choice.
